message.content: In lions, one of the most well‑known dominant traits is the **presence of a mane** in males. The gene(s) that control mane development are expressed in a dominant fashion—if a male inherits the allele for mane growth from either parent, it will typically develop a mane (though its size and density can vary). This dominant trait is what gives male lions their iconic appearance and is a classic example of a dominant phenotype in a wild mammal.
